li-7343164308035358720.text: Two of his four partnerships worked and two hurt, and the difference, he concluded, was whether a partnership agreement existed. He signed his first one in 2016, after a career from a steel plant and metal sales to commercial director of a company with 3,500 employees.

li-7342800662209921024.title: Why do employers hesitate to hire former entrepreneurs?
li-7342800662209921024.text: 44% of employers see entrepreneurial experience as a drawback. The author sees behind it HR's inability to read such a background, the “failed business” label and fear of losing control, and argues for judging the person rather than the stamp on their record.

li-7341717839688388608.title: Why do co-owned businesses run without a partnership agreement?
li-7341717839688388608.text: The author names four types: the cunning (the business is registered to them), the overconfident (“they won't drop me, I'm indispensable”), the naive (“they're my friends”) and the lazy-inexperienced (“too complicated”). With no agreement, you are one of them.

li-7340627143917236225.title: Where should a new partnership begin?
li-7340627143917236225.text: With a portrait of the partner and a written proposal, then a failure scenario and a signed partnership agreement: if the partner refused, the author would not enter the partnership. After that come a scheduled renegotiation date and mutual reporting.

li-7340258936379322368.title: Why does a partnership decay quietly, like a cavity?
li-7340258936379322368.text: It does not burn out suddenly but decays in silence: what was left unsaid builds from discomfort to resentment and silent anger, until all that remains is a break. Prevention is a regular conversation, a partnership agreement and an annual partnership session.

li-7338818695613272064.title: Who decides where venture money goes in the US?
li-7338818695613272064.text: A Stanford study of 22,000+ decision-makers over 25 years found that 79% are men (60% white), 21% are women and 0.8% are Black women. The author advises founders to know this map of power when negotiating with investors.

li-7338102782211616769.title: Why is a founder with no time for reflection a risk to their own business?
li-7338102782211616769.text: At first his energy and vision give the idea life; then inertia, busyness and fear of change start holding everything back, and the company quietly degrades. For the author, reflection is the founders' main function, especially in a partnership.

li-7337729036023992320.title: What makes a partnership work as an exchange?
li-7337729036023992320.text: A partnership is always an exchange of experience, ideas and capital: money without strategy is just glitter, vision without resources is only fog. Honesty and a transparent balance keep profit shared and free of doubts about fairness.

li-7336285669654171650.title: What really lies behind partners' refusal to sign an agreement?
li-7336285669654171650.text: Out loud, partners talk about trust and being busy; underneath, the author sees two motives: fear (of hearing an uncomfortable truth, of losing control) and greed (not sharing, not investing). Strong partners sign out of respect for themselves and each other.

li-7335918019455377410.title: Why does the author see being 40+ as an advantage, not a handicap?
li-7335918019455377410.text: Experience gives context: you see how decisions, risks, the market and people connect, and it is an asset that only appreciates. The median age in the EU in 2024 was 44.7, and by 2050 the workforce in most EU countries will shrink markedly.

li-7335556033269891073.title: Why do the deepest business crises come from silence, not mistakes?
li-7335556033269891073.text: Where a direct conversation is needed, a guess appears; where an agreement is needed, an assumption or silence. The author calls the unsaid a form of passive manipulation; on a recorded talk, one partner regrets they did not speak like this two years earlier.

li-7335191693849169920.title: How do you respond when a partner does not respect your time?
li-7335191693849169920.text: In the case described, three steps worked: a carefully prepared letter to the partner, organisational measures against a repeat, and a separate meeting on one subject only, respect for time. Ignoring another's time, the author says, costs that person part of their life.

li-7333743167336296449.title: What do you do when a partner has reached their level of incompetence?
li-7333743167336296449.text: A co-owner fills up to three roles, owner, manager and executor, and lacks competence in some of them; by the Peter principle, that is where growth stops. The way out: an honest conversation, an assessment of what each really carries, and a reassignment of roles.

li-7333391806392365057.title: Which clients does the author turn down?
li-7333391806392365057.text: Those who want obedience rather than cooperation. The author turned down such a prospective client and works with partners ready to think, listen, respect the other person and reach agreement, not to buy themselves an executor.

li-7333020483350695936.title: Where does a business's money go when it seems to be missing?
li-7333020483350695936.text: Money going missing does not mean it is not there: a business is a system, and the question is who in it ends up holding the margin.

li-7332656272481193984.title: What does a business pay for depending on its founders?
li-7332656272481193984.text: It shows at sale: the more indispensable people and the fewer processes a company has, the less it is worth. In one example from the discussion, cutting that dependence lifted the valuation from 4.2x to 6x EBITDA, so exit from operations and sale scenarios are agreed in advance.

li-7331934210401742848.title: What does maturity mean in a partnership?
li-7331934210401742848.text: Not age, but the ability to see beyond the next step and not run from its consequences. So partners must agree not only on how to split profit but on how to cover losses if it fails: responsibility is the key to trust.

li-7331570093320986626.title: Why does a paid consultation work better than a free one?
li-7331570093320986626.text: In the author's experience, the same words for big money become an action plan, while free ones go in one ear and out the other. Payment creates an obligation to listen, implement and act, and the more a client pays, the more they value what they get.

li-7331206194457378816.title: Why do partnership agreements need updates, like a smartphone?
li-7331206194457378816.text: The company grows, markets and roles change, but the agreements stay the same: partners stop feeling fairness, irritation and tension build, and the end is conflict. For the author, revisiting them is not distrust but responsibility.

li-7330120608963358722.title: Does a partnership always have to be a tandem?
li-7330120608963358722.text: A tandem fixes the roles and limits the scenarios, and the author asks whether it always fits: can partners swap places or rebuild the design from scratch. What it looks like depends only on what they agree.

li-7329396032751013888.title: Can you become well known for the sake of money?
li-7329396032751013888.text: Hardly: popularity is a result of consistency, values, the right moment and the right environment. To earn, build a business; to influence, speak out often and regularly; wanting both means choosing which matters more right now.

li-7329041084603326465.title: Why does a frame of agreements give partners more freedom?
li-7329041084603326465.text: After 20 years coaching Belgium's Olympic team, Alain Goudsmet reached a formula: more frame, more freedom; less frame, more control. Without agreements partners slide into dissatisfaction and control; agreements give a fulcrum for accepted freedom.

li-7328668602390212608.title: What does the story of the Wiz founders who refused $23 billion teach?
li-7328668602390212608.text: Half a year later Google paid $32 billion for Wiz. The author points to synergy and a clear split of roles, founders who are colleagues (10% each), a repeat of an earlier startup's success and a large reserve of trust.

li-7328298129831690242.title: Is there any statistics on business partnership in Ukraine?
li-7328298129831690242.text: A reader poll: the author starts from the claim that no statistics on partnership exist and keeps collecting his own data among a Ukrainian audience. The poll question itself is not quoted in the text.

li-7327581528610242562.title: How can you test a future business partner before committing?
li-7327581528610242562.text: Experienced founders suggest three tests: a joint holiday with families, a small full-cycle project with real money, and a talk about crisis: what to do on failure, conflict or one partner leaving. A rainy-day plan cements trust.

li-7326865918423130112.title: Why do companies look for narrow specialists rather than generalists?
li-7326865918423130112.text: In an age of fast change and information overload, companies value masters deeply immersed in their subject who can deliver a measurable result at once. So an expert focus is easier to notice and draws people into ambitious projects more readily than knowing a bit of everything.

li-7326493672336711680.title: Why does a partnership without detailed agreements end in trouble?
li-7326493672336711680.text: A partnership begins as a mental image, and the gap between that image and reality breeds tension. It is closed through negotiation and a written partnership agreement; friendship, enthusiasm and initial trust are not enough.

li-7326134632393936899.title: What can a toxic reply to a cold first message teach?
li-7326134632393936899.text: From a harsh reply to his profile photo the author drew four lessons: an avatar is recognised in 0.13 seconds, negativity is a litmus test of respect, even toxic feedback is free consulting, and any reply is an act of will.

li-7325768916410986496.title: What is known about partnerships if no statistics exist?
li-7325768916410986496.text: A reader poll from a series in which the author, noting that no statistics on partnership exist, gathers such data himself within the Ukrainian professional network.

tg-73.title: What does having more than two partners add to an IT services company?
tg-73.text: Extra complexity: the partners have to watch how workload and duties are divided. For those building delivery and choosing people, the author recommends the Delivery Happens channel, with cases and irony about IT outsourcing.

li-7325407669723262976.title: Why does a co-owner in an operating role need a bonus, not only dividends?
li-7325407669723262976.text: Without a market valuation of a partner's contribution in a job, conflict gets fertile ground, and replacing them when they leave operations proves costly. A KPI bonus is a company expense; dividends are what remains after all costs and funds.

li-7325043820595695617.title: Why do partners at the start believe they have nothing to agree on?
li-7325043820595695617.text: The honeymoon will end, and partners will have to settle how decisions are made, who answers for what and what to do when plans fail. A partnership without an agreement is building without blueprints, so the best time to write one is when there is nothing yet to divide.

li-7323602991519883264.title: How can you tell a good partner from dead weight?
li-7323602991519883264.text: A good partner is one whose interaction increases the business's options and resources; charm and eloquence do not count. What matters is foreseeing problems and creating resources, and two questions act as filters: what earns my stake, and what earns my partner's?

li-7323224666586734593.title: Why should partners rehearse failure and runaway success in advance?
li-7323224666586734593.text: Scenario planning, a framework dating from 1962, gives partners a pre-agreed course of action for the worst and the best case. In a crisis there is nothing left to negotiate under stress: the scenario has been played out, resources estimated, behaviour agreed.

li-7322875124930478081.title: Why should a co-founder in a working role not go without a salary?
li-7322875124930478081.text: A co-owner can be owner, manager and executor; dividends belong to the first role, while work in the other two is paid. Unpaid work distorts the cost structure and, with a passive partner, leads sooner or later to abuse and conflict.

li-7322509010333515778.title: Why should a partnership session not be measured in hours?
li-7322509010333515778.text: The author dropped hourly billing and sells a solution: a session lasts as long as it takes to reach a partnership agreement the parties are ready to sign. Before it come individual interviews and a question order designed for that specific team.

li-7321414848662151168.title: Do you agree with the author's statement?
li-7321414848662151168.text: A short question to readers: the author asks whether they agree with a statement shown in the image attached to the post.

li-7321062987421704192.title: What makes an unequal partnership of money and idea dangerous?
li-7321062987421704192.text: Without a partnership agreement, whoever has more leverage decides, keeps the key access and contracts, and the idea's author carries the blame for failure. The rules have to be fixed at the start, in a partnership session.

li-7320697667175481344.title: How do you gather statistics on partnerships if none exist?
li-7320697667175481344.text: A reader poll: the author collects such data himself within the Ukrainian professional network and promises regular reports on how it goes and how the collected data can be interpreted.

li-7320335679165476865.title: Why would partners set up a shared pension fund?
li-7320335679165476865.text: At a session three partners agreed to put 10% of net profit into a joint fund, with management rules and an annual audit. Their reasons: long-term motivation and loyalty, and access to assets with high entry thresholds that none could reach alone.

li-7319970038046777345.title: Why does Herbert's Dune read like a report on yesterday's events?
li-7319970038046777345.text: A short note by the author: Frank Herbert's Dune at times seems not science fiction but a documentary report on events of "yesterday".

li-7319261288499429376.title: What does freedom mean for an entrepreneur?
li-7319261288499429376.text: Freedom is being able to let yourself forget what day of the week it is. The author woke without an alarm and cycled for nearly four hours with no headphones or podcasts, declining to follow outside rules, including the demands of social network algorithms.

li-7318526252301058050.title: How do partners know they are ready to step out of operations?
li-7318526252301058050.text: It takes effective delegation, which needs a month for a task, three months for a project and six for a direction. A task is an action, a project a system of actions, a direction a system of thinking and decisions, each level with its own handover procedures.

li-7318152297107066880.title: Why do critical partnership problems stay below the waterline?
li-7318152297107066880.text: By Sidney Yoshida's "iceberg of ignorance" model, most problems are never voiced, and partners lose touch with each other and with the business. The author suggests honest talk, partner meetings, one-on-one feedback and a facilitated session twice a year.

li-7317800300508028928.title: Which nine signs show that a partnership has turned toxic?
li-7317800300508028928.text: Toxic behaviour is rewarded, burnout is the norm, candour is punished, information is hidden and every step is monitored. The chief sign: decent people leave, and those who stay are used to putting up with it or winning at others' expense.

li-7317436441905528832.title: How does funding of future unicorns differ in the early rounds?
li-7317436441905528832.text: Companies that become unicorns raise 3–4 times more capital in every round: $9M against $2M at seed, $105M against $27M at Series C, $304M against $66M at Series G. Causation is unproven, but the correlation is plain.

li-7316347178111660032.title: Why does staying silent set off a delayed conflict in a partnership?
li-7316347178111660032.text: A crack forms not from betrayal but from the unsaid: fear of spoiling the relationship or seeming difficult postpones the conflict and multiplies the tension. The author advises speaking up once discomfort appears and refreshing agreements in a partnership session.

li-7315628397232111618.title: Why set a time limit on the role a partner takes on?
li-7315628397232111618.text: Assigning roles is pointless without agreed terms: "I'll handle marketing" does not say for how long, and the partner may see it differently. The author counted eight questions partners must answer in setting these terms.

li-7315267721934323712.title: What does regular work on a professional network give, and what does it cost?
li-7315267721934323712.text: A Financial Times piece on "superusers" says they build reputation systematically and inquiries come to them; the author confirms clients say "we read your posts". The flip side: noise beyond 15–20 thousand followers and a temptation to oversimplify hard topics.

li-7314898714785939456.title: Who really controls the market of venture-backed unicorns?
li-7314898714785939456.text: Ilya Strebulaev's Stanford study of 1,500 unicorns and over 11,000 investors found six funds holding more than 100 unicorns each, controlling almost 30% of investment. Sequoia Capital leads with 134.

li-7314212683577237504.title: What does a university degree actually guarantee?
li-7314212683577237504.text: The author notes that education, logic and professionalism often do not correlate, though he does not call it a rule. The note ends by asking readers what a university degree is a guarantee of.

li-7313454596348162048.title: What happens when partners skip the agreement to save money?
li-7313454596348162048.text: Three partners (investor, CEO and CTO, split 50/25/25) chose to manage on their own to save budget. Three months later two of them moved to push out the CTO, the season is at risk, and the CEO came back for an agreement between the two remaining.

li-7312721906724483073.title: Does a partner having no plans for the future signal unprofessionalism?
li-7312721906724483073.text: The author asks readers whether a business partner having no plans for the future can count as a sign of unprofessionalism and an inability to run a business.

li-7312360974819205120.title: Can the army become a forge for Ukrainian unicorns?
li-7312360974819205120.text: A Stanford analysis of 2,975 unicorn founders found 42 had served in the Israel Defense Forces, fourth after Google, Microsoft and Stanford. The author suggests a different mindset in military tech could yield Ukrainian unicorns, citing Athlon Avia.

li-7310926523291643906.title: What game are partners playing: incomplete information or transparency?
li-7310926523291643906.text: The author separates Incomplete Information Partnership (IIP), where a partner's motives and plans stay unverified, from Transparent Partnership (TP), where no question is left unanswered. The first breeds friction and a high risk of collapse.

li-7310201934827741184.title: Why agree on a budget before dividing areas of responsibility?
li-7310201934827741184.text: Dividing areas of responsibility makes no sense without rules for forming and approving a budget, since it is unclear whether there is money to deliver on the commitment. Two partners fell out because one assumed a website costs $300 and the other arrived with a $2,500 budget.

li-7309841893016690689.title: Why do investors bet on the founding team rather than the product?
li-7309841893016690689.text: Products change, founders' qualities do not. The game Glitch (2011) burned $17.5 million of investor money, yet Accel kept its stake: the team's internal tool became Slack, acquired by Salesforce for $27 billion.

li-7308390557137989632.title: What are the warning signs that a partner is stealing from the company?
li-7308390557137989632.text: Three groups of signs: a lifestyle beyond known income, unjustified workaholism (insisting on doing tasks alone, refusing to delegate or take leave) and documentary chaos. Specialists estimate that in 89% of partner thefts at least two of these signs were present beforehand.

li-7307667975736553472.title: How do you avoid learning of a partner's holiday once he is on the beach?
li-7307667975736553472.text: The author often hears complaints about a co-owner who plans his leave as an owner would, so the others find out after the fact. It is irritating for sure, but in the author's words easy to prevent in advance.

li-7307305801671450624.title: Why does the road to a unicorn call for agreements worked out early?
li-7307305801671450624.text: Becoming a unicorn takes 6.6 years on average and many rounds: 91% pass Series B and 21% become unicorns at Series D, while 33% of seed-funded startups never reach the next round. Hence co-founders need worked-out agreements, ideally a signed partnership agreement.

li-7306222327753539585.title: How much money will the partners take out of the business?
li-7306222327753539585.text: The author calls it the most important question, since a business partnership is set up to make money. To answer it, a series of financial planning questions has to be settled first.

li-7305856941640052740.title: Can a partnership agreement indicate the quality of business partners?
li-7305856941640052740.text: An agreement shows partners can negotiate: they understand timing, duties, responsibility and consequences of breach. If a company runs on spoken words, its promises to clients will likely stay spoken too; per HBR, clear expectation-setters earn 25% more.

li-7305129515347767296.title: Why do some partners grow 2-3x a year while others argue about money?
li-7305129515347767296.text: The author names a shared financial vision as the main reason. If one partner wants to reinvest and the other to draw dividends, constant arguments drain energy and threaten a split; without agreeing on money at the start, a quarrel over it is inevitable.

li-7304767906775494656.title: Is it true that unicorns are huge corporations?
li-7304767906775494656.text: No: a Stanford study led by Ilya Strebulaev found that 46% of unicorns employ fewer than 500 people and another 30% between 500 and 1,000. The author expects AI and automation to make unicorn teams even smaller.

li-7304097020468715520.title: Why is trust built slowly and lost in an instant?
li-7304097020468715520.text: The author shares the thought that trust takes a long, hard effort to build and is lost in a moment.

li-7302592526551519234.title: How did the youngest partner persuade the others to pay for his MBA?
li-7302592526551519234.text: At a session of three partners (62, 47 and 38) the youngest proposed a package: he runs operations, the eldest retires gradually, the company pays for his MBA and he commits to seven years afterwards. The partners agreed: investing in your own person beats hunting for talent.

li-7302229390837321728.title: Do you need a formal education to found a unicorn?
li-7302229390837321728.text: Per Stanford GSB, unicorn founders are twice as likely as the average American over 25 to hold a bachelor's degree, three times a master's and six times a doctorate, and five times less likely to lack higher education. Gates is, the author says, an exception.

li-7301145103698477056.title: Why does the author not reschedule after a client's no-show?
li-7301145103698477056.text: In 90% of cases he does not hold the meeting again: a no-show usually means no pressing need, disorganisation, or neglect of a chance to warn of changed plans. Those who did not warn but ask for a new meeting (about 10%) get one only if they pay for it.

li-7300780566612750337.title: Why do most partnerships work like a black box?
li-7300780566612750337.text: There are almost no books, courses, schools or statistics on partnership, so it forms at random, and when problems arise partners cannot locate their source. The author holds that even basic agreements jotted on a napkin are worth more than no documentation at all.

li-7300416853405786112.title: What happens to a partner's share and family if he dies with nothing agreed?
li-7300416853405786112.text: With no agreed value of business and shares the family is left with nothing: in a real case the company turned loss-making after a partner's death and his widow was asked to cover a share of the debts. The author advises an annual valuation and an internal declaration.

li-7300057402249248768.title: At what stage is it still not too late for partners to agree?
li-7300057402249248768.text: Three levels: "we trust each other" (the best time to agree), "something went wrong" (still not too late, but most postpone) and "sort out this chaos" (mediators and courts needed). Those who settle it at level one never reach level three.

li-7299692683269177344.title: Do you need an MBA to build a unicorn?
li-7299692683269177344.text: No: a Stanford GSB study found an MBA held by 424 of 2,975 unicorn founders, or 14%. 112 business schools have produced at least one such founder, but the six top schools account for over half of the MBA holders.

li-7298609275453493249.title: Why does a partner's extreme sport obsession worry investors?
li-7298609275453493249.text: Investors look at people too, and any co-owner dependency, even a sporting one, is a red flag. The person turns unpredictable, risk-prone and less critical, while training takes 15-18 hours a week and time and money drift away from the business.

li-7297877524728995840.title: Which partner has the right to call himself the boss in the market?
li-7297877524728995840.text: A partner approached the author: a co-owner tells everyone behind their backs that he is in charge and the others decide nothing. Asked whether they had ever agreed who may position themselves how in the market, the answer was the expected one: no.

li-7297517803819929600.title: Is there statistics on partnership agreements, as there is on prenups?
li-7297517803819929600.text: No: 2,762 prenuptial contracts were registered in 2024 (up 7% on 2023), one per 54 marriages, while data on partnership agreements does not exist. The author calls such an agreement insurance: it fixes profit split, exit, roles and the consequences of bad faith.

li-7297155587212021760.title: What did the founders of unicorns most often study?
li-7297155587212021760.text: Ilya Strebulaev of Stanford analysed almost 2,200 unicorn founders: 95% hold a bachelor's degree, and Computer Science, Engineering and Economics account for 53% of all degrees. The sample spans 47 majors, from theology to anthropology.

li-7296072229912502273.title: What pulls co-founders apart when each has a different vision of growth?
li-7296072229912502273.text: Some want to stay small and boutique, others to keep full control, others to scale fast, and the result is conflict, delayed decisions and power struggles. Successful co-founders agree in advance on risk limits, expansion plans and an exit strategy.

li-7295708510334451712.title: How do you split equity when partners contribute unequally?
li-7295708510334451712.text: Mike Moyer's Slicing Pie model allocates equity dynamically: each contribution earns points with a multiplier, and a share is its percentage of all points. In the worked example the investor with $30,000 gets 57% and the specialist with work and clients 43%.

li-7295351773664309249.title: Which decisions should partners make together?
li-7295351773664309249.text: The list of joint decisions should be set at the start of the relationship, along with how they are made: consensus or majority, whether a share equals votes, what happens on disagreement, and which matters belong to a partner or CEO alone.

li-7294981519842897920.title: What are the odds of finding a business partner who fits a given profile?
li-7294981519842897920.text: Multiplying the population shares for each criterion of the profile (gender, region, age, education, leadership experience, IT) gives odds of about 0.0002%. The author concludes that finding such a partner is great luck, so the search is best started early.

li-7294619343819083777.title: Should founders spend their energy on a name and a logo?
li-7294619343819083777.text: No. The author mocks the claim that renamed companies are 7.5% more likely to become unicorns: Zimride became Lyft and Facebook became Meta as they grew. The investment belongs in the business and in the partners' relationship.

li-7293995637811867648.title: What do founders advise other founders?
li-7293995637811867648.text: A short note: the author's library is growing, and he is curious what founders advise other founders in it.

li-7293530729370587136.title: Does regular reporting strengthen a partnership?
li-7293530729370587136.text: Yes: between partners, reporting works as transparency rather than control, removing grounds for doubt and suspicion. The author advises agreeing on it from the start and discussing finances, each partner's contribution and progress on tasks.

tg-20.title: How does trust in a relationship affect the speed of work?
tg-20.text: When there is trust in a relationship, people move on to implementation very quickly.

li-7293267090898092032.title: Is a personal brand a stake in a business?
li-7293267090898092032.text: An announcement of a live talk on 6 February at 4 p.m. on the topic: is a personal brand a share in a business, and how does social capital work and what does it cost.

li-7293169124275294208.title: What do marriage and divorce figures in Ukraine show?
li-7293169124275294208.text: Ukraine's Ministry of Justice reports 150,200 marriages and 141,800 divorces, a near 1:1 ratio, the closest in recent history. No such statistics exist for business partnerships, and the author asks readers whether they see a link.

li-7292812067944734721.title: What can you do when a partner acts like the sole owner?
li-7292812067944734721.text: If partners never agreed on how each may present themselves to the team, there is nothing to hold such behaviour against: no boundary was set. In a client's case, one co-owner routes every issue through himself, does not report and instructs other partners' staff.

li-7292436742408736769.title: Why does the author compare a partnership session to vaccination?
li-7292436742408736769.text: By IMF estimates, vaccinating 60% of humanity would add about $9 trillion to world GDP for $50 billion; a partnership session is the partnership's vaccine, the agreement its passport. No partnership statistics are kept; Wasserman finds 65% of ventures fail over partner conflict.

li-7292105224645705728.title: Where will the author speak on business partnership?
li-7292105224645705728.text: The author announces that the next day he will speak at the event "Business partnership: from a business idea to a key asset of the business".

li-7292082133945184256.title: What experience do unicorn founders most often have?
li-7292082133945184256.text: Ilya Strebulaev's analysis shows 60% of unicorns have at least one experienced entrepreneur among their founders, and many came from Google, Microsoft, R&D and top management. The author's formula: startup experience, corporate expertise, technical knowledge.

li-7290998848221540352.title: Why is a lack of disagreement between partners a warning sign?
li-7290998848221540352.text: If there is no disagreement, one partner is probably adding no value: a partnership's strength is its range of views. Disagreement is productive with clear roles, transparency, and a focus on improving the business rather than on winning the argument.

li-7290631786412318722.title: Why do some partners refuse to put agreements down?
li-7290631786412318722.text: 66% of partners have no agreements at all, and the author sees two reasons for resisting them: a childlike failure to grasp the consequences, or a deliberate wish to manipulate the partner. The only way out is to agree and sign a partnership agreement.

li-7290268439615569920.title: How should partners agree on leaving the business in advance?
li-7290268439615569920.text: The question "How will we part ways?" belongs at the start of a relationship: in a partnership session the author asks it right after the first round of share allocation. Clear exit rules keep partners from being hostages of a partnership with no lawful way out.

li-7289911564902567936.title: How can a hired executive win an equity stake in a business?
li-7289911564902567936.text: On the eve of a final interview with the owner, a CEO candidate used a session to build a negotiation strategy: an owner profile, a self-portrait, matching and risk zones, and answers on stake, guarantees and KPIs. He aimed for 50% and received 10%.

li-7289544526967312384.title: What did the author conclude after his social network account was locked?
li-7289544526967312384.text: Six conclusions after five days without his main social network: digital assets vanish at one button press, followers belong to the platform (486 disappeared), diversification is needed, and the real audience is subscribers of a newsletter and one's own channel.

li-7287372040804651008.title: Do you need a partner in order to finally start your own business?
li-7287372040804651008.text: No: a client wanted a partner to structure his time and was ready to give 50% of a business projected to earn 700-800 thousand euros a year. After advice to hire an employee on KPIs he stayed sole owner and kept 350 thousand euros.

li-7287012087904555008.title: How long after the first venture money does a startup become a unicorn?
li-7287012087904555008.text: On average 4.5 years after the first venture funding, per Ilya Strebulaev's analysis of 1,516 US unicorns: the peak is year five (123 companies), and 88 made it in under a year. Without clear agreements between founders, such a marathon cannot be run.

li-7285558055348396033.title: What is an idea worth in a partnership?
li-7285558055348396033.text: An idea alone is rarely worth much: value comes from the work of implementing and validating it. Illustration: a businessman listened to someone's idea, quietly implemented it and simply thanked the person who had shared it.

li-7285196912683569152.title: How, and on what terms, should one leave a partnership?
li-7285196912683569152.text: If a partnership has no map showing the exit, the only way out is to destroy it, so the terms are easier to agree in advance. Put on paper how long each partner stays and what one gets for leaving earlier or later than the agreed term.

li-7284837767564464128.title: What should an owner put in writing before giving a top manager a stake?
li-7284837767564464128.text: Eight items for the partnership agreement: reporting, terms and appointment of managers, audit, company valuation, meetings, internal control and the right to launch checks. Basis: in 82% of fraud cases top managers are suspected, in 10% business partners.

li-7284473549635936256.title: How much do investors earn from unicorn startups?
li-7284473549635936256.text: On average 3,100% on invested capital, according to a Stanford study (Strebulaev) of 1,516 venture-backed American unicorns. 45 companies returned 50x and only 21 fell below their initial investment; mergers and acquisitions bring 4,900%, IPOs 2,700%.

li-7284133399919792128.title: Is making money together the only basis of a partnership?
li-7284133399919792128.text: A question to readers: the author suspects that partners' motivation runs deeper than earning money together and asks whether others agree.

li-7283419821847797761.title: Why don't verbal agreements between partners work?
li-7283419821847797761.text: Partners are people too: they take in 65% of information visually, 30% by ear and 5% through experience, and they forget or twist what was said. Agreements belong in writing in a partnership agreement, with a revision of it agreed upfront.

li-7283023757282078721.title: Why draw up an ideal partner profile before starting a business?
li-7283023757282078721.text: 95% of entrepreneurs enter a partnership through friendship, family or chance contacts; only 5% use the Ideal Partner Profile framework. It helps assess one's own resources soberly and see what a partner must compensate; a 60-question questionnaire goes with it.

li-7282660494434328576.title: What do investors look for in startup founders?
li-7282660494434328576.text: The founders' personality: due diligence, the ability to defend a position and hear arguments, referrals and personal meetings before investing. The author sees a partnership agreement as a "founder's licence", proof that co-founders can actually reach agreements.

li-7282302702041153536.title: How should co-owners report to one another?
li-7282302702041153536.text: Co-owners usually also run the company, so they are owners and employees at once. The author asks how partners should agree on mutual reporting when an owner seems to owe nobody an account.

li-7281938337559433216.title: How long does it take a startup to become a unicorn?
li-7281938337559433216.text: On average 6.6 years, per an analysis of 1,044 companies (Strebulaev, Stanford): the peak is years 3 to 8, and after year 10 success stories thin out. Unicorns most often have two or three founders with clear agreements.

li-7280275102238146560.title: What makes a consulting session productive?
li-7280275102238146560.text: A prepared client: the author asked in advance for a case description and a brief, and the detailed write-up made it possible to go deeper into the nuances and do more than planned. A thank-you note for feedback on that work.

li-7279401353280409600.title: What did the author's first year of public writing teach?
li-7279401353280409600.text: Starting from zero on 4 June 2024, the author found that English posts and two a week achieved nothing, and that running several networks at once is unrealistic. Focusing on one, he wrote 179 posts, held 30+ interviews with leads and won 9 clients.

li-7278308473593827328.title: What does an ideal business partner look like?
li-7278308473593827328.text: Anonymous surveys put the ability to negotiate and reflect first (71%), then being sensible and responsible (61%). The author's formula: a person with different resources and competences but the same values and principles.

li-7277954877140455424.title: Can a company come back after losing 2.1 billion of investor money?
li-7277954877140455424.text: Lilium, which laid off over a thousand staff in December, announced a deal with an investor consortium on 24 December: the new owners will buy the subsidiaries' assets, and the founders get no money. The author's takeaway: look for a lucky partner, clever ones can be hired.

li-7277224390604259328.title: Who appoints the CEO in a company with several partners?
li-7277224390604259328.text: A question for discussion: as a company grows, its partners sooner or later consider appointing a CEO from the staff or from outside. The author asks how partners should agree on this.

li-7275779833593253888.title: Why should partners hold a strategy session at the start or end of a year?
li-7275779833593253888.text: To align vision and goals, review results and acknowledge each other's contribution. The author suggests starting with quarterly sessions and a written exercise: note what you value in a partner, their unexpected contribution and their impact on the business.

li-7275414162451689474.title: How often does a co-founder leave a startup in its first years?
li-7275414162451689474.text: Carta data (13,133 startups, 2015-2024) show that in 25% of venture-backed startups a founder leaves within four years, before the stake has vested. Hence the case for a vesting schedule, a plan for a founder's exit and a partnership agreement.

li-7275052304221822976.title: How do you avoid a falling-out with a partner when building a business abroad?
li-7275052304221822976.text: A shared language and a kindred spirit do not replace an agreement under stress. Four rules: discuss roles and areas of responsibility, put agreements in writing, review them regularly and set the format and frequency of communication.

li-7274687557362212864.title: Is a share in the company always equal to a share in the profit?
li-7274687557362212864.text: No: with 50/50 ownership, profit may split 80/20 in the investor's favour until the investment is repaid, then the restaurateur's share grows to 55 and 60%. The investor gets income and the restaurateur stays motivated to keep working.

li-7274326789164781569.title: Who most often founds unicorns in the US?
li-7274326789164781569.text: White men: 75% of founders against 29% of the population; about 14 men for every woman founder. Only Asian founders exceed their population share (17.5% vs 6.4%). Stanford data on 1,110 companies, 1997-2021.

li-7273235223197155328.title: Why do partnerships fall apart even when they start well?
li-7273235223197155328.text: Because of seven unresolved issues: no shared goal, weak communication, unclear roles, mismatched expectations, ignored conflicts, uncoordinated decisions and no adaptation to change. For each the author gives a fix, from shared values to regular review of agreements.

li-7272873798205349888.title: Is it worth making a top manager a partner?
li-7272873798205349888.text: Yes, if the owner is willing to share equity: it retains a key person, raises motivation and gives the company a partner who thinks like an owner. Signs of readiness: initiative, over three years in the company, willingness to buy a stake or earn it from profit.

li-7272512374010499072.title: What should founders agree on before they start working together?
li-7272512374010499072.text: Six subjects: roles and areas of responsibility, goals and expectations, finances, decision-making, conflicts and exit. The logic comes from Gallup research: companies with the most engaged employees earn 147% more profit per share.

li-7272152660735102977.title: What if a voting partner is out of reach for a long time?
li-7272152660735102977.text: This should be settled in advance: can the remaining partners take an urgent decision without him. By the author's estimate there are over 150 such procedural questions to cover in a partnership session.

li-7271787238043045888.title: Do unicorn companies often fail?
li-7271787238043045888.text: Rarely: of American unicorns as of 2020, 26 failed (including Theranos, FTX and VICE Media), 756 stayed private and 1,264 exited. Drawing on Stanford data, the author treats a $1 billion valuation as a good predictor of survival.

li-7270701023147565056.title: How can you tell people are only playing at partnership?
li-7270701023147565056.text: Five signs: they act on assumptions, financial obligations breed conflict, roles and decision processes are undefined, and there is no exit strategy. The author argues a partnership agreement turns the game into professional cooperation.

li-7270338678449745921.title: How do you make any partnership of yours effective?
li-7270338678449745921.text: A short lead-in to an instruction document on making a partnership work; the steps themselves are not in the text and are in the attached file.

li-7269976369688686594.title: Why did the Wiz founders turn down $23 billion from Google?
li-7269976369688686594.text: They chose independence and their own route to an IPO. The author credits the group's strength to clear roles, shared service in Unit 8200, equal 10% stakes and the earlier success of their joint startup Adallom.

li-7269613893281271811.title: Why ask partners a thousand questions?
li-7269613893281271811.text: The technique comes from improv theatre: a character gains depth only when the questions run out. Where awkward questions are not asked, a partnership stays flat and uncertain, so at a partnership session the author has partners answer them up front.

li-7269251240994197504.title: How much does a business partnership resemble a marriage?
li-7269251240994197504.text: In the US, charts of marriage length and of startup exit times nearly match, though the author sees no causal link. What matters more: for over half of startups the road to exit takes more than 8 years, so expectations and an exit strategy must be agreed at the start.

li-7268164407409459200.title: Which five partnership rules did the author draw from 14 years of experience?
li-7268164407409459200.text: Discuss everything up front, put it in writing, raise disagreements early, revisit terms as the business grows and agree a civilised exit. The rules rest on the author's own climb from 5% to 50% of a company over 12 years and on client cases.

li-7267802067803541504.title: How does the number of co-founders affect each one's exit value?
li-7267802067803541504.text: In a Stanford GSB analysis of 606 US unicorns, each added co-founder cuts net exit value per person by about 32%: from $2.1 billion for a solo founder to under $0.5 billion each at six or more.

li-7267439532550062080.title: Is the goal of leaving day-to-day operations always sound?
li-7267439532550062080.text: If the partners' end goal is lying under a palm tree, outstanding results rarely follow, so at a session it is a cue to ask what they really want. The author's example is Elon Musk, who with a fortune near $200 billion lived at his factories beside his team for years.

li-7267077161021304833.title: Why do some partners take risks while others play safe?
li-7267077161021304833.text: It is motives, not personality types: a startup founder's loss is capped while the upside is not, whereas a corporate manager risks bonuses and career. What co-founders need is not different people but aligned motives.

li-7266726711105363968.title: Is a partner worth a second chance?
li-7266726711105363968.text: The question comes down to whether the partner can change, tested by three questions: are both ready for a mature dialogue and a mature conflict, and is the offender capable of sincere remorse. A single "no" means a loop of "continue or part ways".

li-7265627643763425280.title: What is an emergent partnership and when does it arise?
li-7265627643763425280.text: It is a partnership whose result exceeds the sum of its contributions. It takes readiness to adapt, strong trust, regular meaningful contact, new solutions born of the partnership's dynamics and fixed agreements; the author's model is the founders of Nova Poshta.

li-7265265230232907779.title: How can a partnership avoid collapse when shares are equal?
li-7265265230232907779.text: The Agile Partnership model ties shares to results: define each person's contribution, set measurable goals, issue conditional shares and allocate them on outcomes. That brings transparency, objectivity and flexibility if someone fails to deliver.

li-7264902894150164482.title: What does Lilium's bankruptcy teach about building a partner team?
li-7264902894150164482.text: In a "how to fail" format the author dissects a company that raised $2.1 billion: four young engineers with identical skills, no outside view and no experience of failure, but big names alongside and a supply contract without a working prototype.

li-7264540489490554882.title: What belongs in a partnership agreement under bill 9103?
li-7264540489490554882.text: Bill 9103 states that partnership is not marriage, and there is no case practice yet, so the author advises spelling out terms in a detailed agreement. Ten blocks: property, health, care, housing, debts, termination, representation, confidentiality, term and disputes.

li-7264178974954508288.title: Why are conflicts between partners inevitable, and how can they be prevented?
li-7264178974954508288.text: People enter partnerships without knowing the rules, and friendly trust is no substitute for agreements. Disappointment equals reality minus expectations, so expectations must be discussed at the start, and each partner should ask how they would part if things go wrong.

li-7263091014570045440.title: How can you stay fit without a gym and without losing time?
li-7263091014570045440.text: The author trains at home with kettlebells, which help keep strength, flexibility and endurance and counter age-related loss of muscle mass. Time is his most expensive resource, so during workouts he listens to podcasts and audiobooks.

li-7262728643213250561.title: Can a partnership be built on the principle of service?
li-7262728643213250561.text: The author carries servant leadership over to co-owners: each helps strengthen the other's strengths. He leans on data that a manager affects mental health as much as a spouse, and suggests one test question to a partner: how can I help you improve your results?

li-7262366232782274561.title: What do partners in post-Soviet countries agree on?
li-7262366232782274561.text: Most often shares and profit (36%), roles (32%) and strategy (22%), and only 27% of partnerships get through their life cycle without major conflicts. For agreeing on their own, the author compiled 20 questions in four groups.

li-7262003852059557888.title: Why do people really enter a partnership?
li-7262003852059557888.text: Beyond economics the author names four motives: a need for stimulation, for structuring time, for closeness, and nostalgia. When partners play different games conflict is bound to follow, so each should recognise their own motive and say it aloud.

li-7261641474096685057.title: Is it worth signing a partnership agreement?
li-7261641474096685057.text: An ironic "no" built on five arguments: flexibility, savings, trust, easy dispute resolution and avoiding awkward questions. The anchor figure: 66% of partners have no agreements at all, written or spoken.

li-7260554302320955392.title: How do you know that this person is your partner?
li-7260554302320955392.text: Twenty questions for a candidate and for yourself: what binds us, what do I lack, what does my trust rest on, what happens if our paths part. The list ends by asking who they are: a match, a coal or water.

li-7260191931949887489.title: What is trust between partners made of?
li-7260191931949887489.text: A partnership is 100% relationships and relationships are 100% trust, and the author boils trust down to twelve everyday acts: arrive on time, tell the truth, keep promises, ask for feedback, respect boundaries. Trust is not built in a day.

li-7259830808029356032.title: Why do broken expectations and surprise breed partner conflicts?
li-7259830808029356032.text: Conflict builds when expectations are broken and news arrives suddenly. In a nightclub case, a co-owner in charge of a delayed renovation announces a holiday three days ahead, and both sides have a logic of their own; a session and an agreement defused it.

li-7259467130583072769.title: Why doesn't an equal split of shares between co-founders work?
li-7259467130583072769.text: The author holds that 99% of co-founders split shares equally and get it wrong, because an equal split follows no rule. Each brings three kinds of capital, human, economic and social, and weighs them differently, so shares have to be calculated.

li-7259104914100895744.title: Where does Ukraine rank by founders of unicorns?
li-7259104914100895744.text: By absolute count, 12 founders, Ukraine ranks 10th, and per million inhabitants, 0.32 founders, it ranks 6th. The author calculated this from a Stanford GSB study, in which almost half of unicorn founders were born outside the US.

li-7258017600759054337.title: How does a partner's spouse affect decisions in a shared business?
li-7258017600759054337.text: You stop talking to your partner and start talking to a projection of the conversations at home about you, with the spouse competing through the partner. The author reads this as a signal to agree and put it on paper at once.

li-7257655188327460865.title: What do co-founders need to agree on before they start?
li-7257655188327460865.text: The author prepared a 16-page partnership agreement template with 18 sections: roles, equity split, vesting, IP, compensation, exit, death or incapacity, disputes, governing law. His starting point is that co-founders rarely know what to discuss.

li-7257296054788706304.title: Can partners agree on a day off in the middle of the week?
li-7257296054788706304.text: The author first met such an arrangement in 2018: one co-owner insisted on a four-day week with Wednesday off, and the other, after trying it, agreed the results were better. He advises agreeing on this rhythm in advance and writing it into the partnership agreement.

li-7256930426462584833.title: What experience did unicorn founders have before founding the company?
li-7256930426462584833.text: A Stanford GSB analysis of 2,507 founders of venture-backed US unicorns found that 22% had founded companies before, 19% were vice presidents or directors, 13% worked in technical roles and 10% were CEOs. The author advises choosing partners with such a background.

li-7256568030527115265.title: Why could the partners not merge even though they saw the benefit?
li-7256568030527115265.text: The third participant would not compromise: he grew up an only child with no experience of sharing or settling. The merger fell through, which the author sees as a good outcome; he says that in 20% of cases partners decide after a session not to go into business together.

li-7255096125483798529.title: What should partners do when their relationship hits a crisis?
li-7255096125483798529.text: Breaking up is an extreme exit and usually far from optimal. A crisis means the old rules no longer work: boundaries and expectations have to be redefined and recorded, and with skilled negotiation the new agreement works better than the old one.

li-7254733776591712256.title: Why do partners have no written agreements, and what does it cost them?
li-7254733776591712256.text: In 90% of cases a partnership rests on trust with nothing in writing: no split of responsibility or losses, no exit scenario, no rules for bad faith, no dispute mechanism. The author offers six steps and a step-by-step Partner Journey Map.

li-7254372339449024513.title: What positions do founders hold in unicorn companies?
li-7254372339449024513.text: According to Stanford GSB data (Ilya Strebulaev, 2024) on 1,110 companies, 34% of founders are CEOs, 16% each chair the board or are vice presidents, 13% are CTOs, 12% presidents and 4% COOs. The study found 198 unique job titles.

li-7254009258545926146.title: How many monitors does work actually take?
li-7254009258545926146.text: The author jokingly traces his path from three monitors in 2012 to six after buying 4K screens, then back to four: a central one, one above it and two vertical side screens. Multitasking is handled by moving the eyes, not by switching windows.

li-7252974358199975936.title: What does The Shawshank Redemption teach about partnership?
li-7252974358199975936.text: Andy and Red's alliance rests on trust, mutual help and shared goals: Andy brings the ideas and the plan, Red helps him adapt and believes in the plan. Such a partnership, the author says, can pull people out of the deepest pits.

li-7252921792145620992.title: What makes up the formula for success in a partnership?
li-7252921792145620992.text: Three parts: the idea, the execution and the partnership agreement. Without the agreement the result is chaos, without execution procrastination, without the idea routine; success appears when all three work together.

li-7252659698120744960.title: Why does the author prefer to work with partners in person?
li-7252659698120744960.text: Most communication today happens online, but the author prefers working in person, even when it means a long journey.

li-7252559385531404288.title: Why put a partnership deal on paper if lawyers exist?
li-7252559385531404288.text: A partnership agreement is the outcome of a partnership session and can serve as the brief for lawyers drafting a shareholders agreement. Far from everything can be formalised legally, and it is often the only document recording that the partners agreed.

li-7252197025029472258.title: Why do Ukrainian owners not give hired directors a stake?
li-7252197025029472258.text: Only 2% of directors hold a small stake, and the share of founder-directors rose from 64% in 2021 to 72.7% in 2024. The author sees weak management motivation here and names the option as an alternative: not a stake, but a path to one.

li-7251834616876077056.title: Why are bronze medallists happier than silver medallists?
li-7251834616876077056.text: In Richard Wiseman's study The Luck Factor, bronze medallists think they could have won nothing, while silver medallists think they could have taken gold. Psychologists call this ability to imagine what might have happened counterfactual thinking.

li-7251472242792878080.title: How can a two-partner exit dispute be settled in one evening?
li-7251472242792878080.text: The author's mediation terms: three separate rooms, no time limit, the parties' usual comfort, no alcohol, unlimited food. After interviews and a joint session, the parties wrote out by hand, at 1 a.m., an agreement with the sum, payment schedule and deferred terms.

li-7250422586029854720.title: What does The Grand Budapest Hotel say about business relationships?
li-7250422586029854720.text: As soon as the partner-heroes had a plan for a shared future, they set out the terms, drew up a partnership agreement and signed it; their success rests on faith in what was agreed. The author calls this a lost culture of business relations.

li-7250385116131188736.title: How can partners keep disappointment from wrecking the relationship?
li-7250385116131188736.text: Through communication, meaning systematic mutual immersion in context, and through cooperation: own what you control and bring the rest to joint discussion. The closer expectations are to reality, the lower the potential for disappointment.

li-7250083109654736896.title: Why is an appeal to authority not an argument in a dispute?
li-7250083109654736896.text: Even a recognised expert's opinion must be backed by facts, logic or evidence: a person's status does not make their words correct. Such an appeal is a logical fallacy, argumentum ad verecundiam, and a dispute should turn on the substance of the arguments.

li-7250022686842642433.title: Where does disappointment between business partners come from?
li-7250022686842642433.text: From expectations colliding with reality: the company lacks resources for one partner's project, there is no profit for the dividends expected, a partner is moved to a new direction. So partners need to identify and soften disappointment and manage it.

li-7249670828760436737.title: Why must partners manage disappointment as well as expectations?
li-7249670828760436737.text: Disappointment is expectation minus reality: it breeds resentment and anger and sets off the four horsemen that wreck relationships: contempt, criticism, stonewalling and threats. The quality of a partnership depends on managing both expectations and disappointment.

li-7249309462677622785.title: What did a food producer and an investor agree on at a partnership session?
li-7249309462677622785.text: Starting equity of 35/65, moving to 50/50 after three consecutive months of operating profit, follow-on investment terms, and joint decisions on goals, share sales, investment and new markets. Heirs receive the value of the share, not a say in management.

li-7248995944438939648.title: What should co-founders do if they dare not set their boundaries?
li-7248995944438939648.text: A short note for co-founders who dare not define their own boundaries or put hard questions to a partner. The author offers help with how to do it.

li-7248935507554930688.title: Why do co-founders quarrel, and how do clear expectations prevent it?
li-7248935507554930688.text: The author holds that co-founders quarrel because they cannot manage disappointment and satisfaction. His model of clear expectations is Churchill's speech of 13 May 1940: no promises or abstractions, so any result better than expected counts as a win.

li-7247848331979149312.title: Why must a partnership proposal be written for a specific reader?
li-7247848331979149312.text: In the film Henry Fool the same lines of a poem move one listener to tears and outrage another. So the proposal to a partner, a part of the business plan, needs a portrait of that partner, so that it reaches the right hands.

li-7247652067945660416.title: How can a founder talk to an audience and reach business goals?
li-7247652067945660416.text: An announcement of a talk with a guest about a founder's personal brand: how to hold a dialogue with the audience and achieve business goals through it.

li-7247485946596646912.title: What lies behind the phrase "I am in charge of logistics"?
li-7247485946596646912.text: Nothing: the phrase seems clear, the listener agrees and moves on. Written agreements guard against such generalities, because once partners have to put it on paper they stop accepting wording that says nothing.

li-7247123509280165891.title: Why do oral agreements fail once a partner needs nothing more from the other?
li-7247123509280165891.text: Two people launched a project, discussed terms orally and wrote nothing down; once it earned hundreds of thousands, the one in control called the other's investment a loan. The session and agreement have to happen while the partner still wants the cooperation.

li-7246761180248031233.title: How does the Thomas theorem explain conflicts between partners?
li-7246761180248031233.text: If people define a situation as real, it is real in its consequences: when partners' perceptions diverge, each acts in a reality of their own and turns defensive. Regular structured dialogue, such as a partnership session, is the hygiene of a partnership.

li-7246398798401294338.title: Which phrase shows that a partnership is under threat?
li-7246398798401294338.text: "We agreed on everything at the start": it means there are no real agreements that anyone is ready to keep. Agreements should be a product with an expiry date: renewed at least yearly, covering life scenarios, and revised as often as needed.

li-7245311644732448769.title: What does the film Twelve Monkeys say about a partner's "crazy ideas"?
li-7245311644732448769.text: The film's hero, whom the psychiatrists take for a patient, is telling the plain truth about the future. The author suggests not judging too harshly a partner who arrives with yet another crazy idea: he may simply have come from the future.

li-7244586871639429120.title: Why ask partners at a partnership session how they want things to be?
li-7244586871639429120.text: Few partners can say how they want things to be, yet all can say how they do not; without the first answer there is no basis for cooperation. The author opens a session with it, so expectations are described early and most conflicts avoided.

li-7244228276544524288.title: How should partners agree on the balance between work and personal life?
li-7244228276544524288.text: In a separate section of the partnership agreement: working hours, reply times, total vacation and the order of vacations. For example, 50 hours a week for the first six months, a reply within two hours, 6 weeks of vacation a year.

li-7243862109527175169.title: Can you take a partnership for a test drive before entering it?
li-7243862109527175169.text: Yes: the 1993 experiment by Ambady and Rosenthal showed that we judge a person within minutes and hold on to that first impression. A trial period of joint work tests compatibility, competence, reliability and financial discipline.

li-7242790018681888768.title: What does the film about Facebook's creation say about partnership?
li-7242790018681888768.text: The story of Facebook shows how ideas, personal ambition and working at the limit of endurance turn into a global project. Partnerships and agreements between the founders are key elements of the plot.

li-7242412508853002241.title: How could Zuckerberg have answered a congressman's manipulative question?
li-7242412508853002241.text: The question "Do you want to apologise to the families?" leaves no good answer: refusing looks like indifference, apologising like admitting guilt. The author suggests silently standing up and leaving, then stating the position live an hour later, free of pressure.

li-7242104468098453504.title: What does the author say about partnership on the podcast?
li-7242104468098453504.text: A recorded conversation about business partnership for the SaaS Founders podcast; the video is available via the link.

li-7242050149865148416.title: What does a business pay for not having a signed partnership agreement?
li-7242050149865148416.text: An investor with resources to spare does not put them into the shared business because he distrusts the managing partner: nothing was agreed at the start, and there are no reports. By his estimate the business could be three times bigger.

li-7241687769243103233.title: What must a partnership not be built from if it is to take off?
li-7241687769243103233.text: Not from oral agreements and formulas like "it goes without saying", "we'll sort it out when a problem comes" or "decent people will agree". Such a partnership will not take off; the author counts the ability to avoid building this way as a superpower.

li-7241340779128901634.title: Where does the move from C-level manager to partner of the owner begin?
li-7241340779128901634.text: With stating your own goals: why you want an equity stake rather than a bigger bonus. The next steps are to show unique value, find ways to grow the pie, review results with the owner, scale what works and strengthen trust.

li-7240253294244212737.title: What is the danger of a secretive partner you trust unconditionally?
li-7240253294244212737.text: A classic about financial machinations and ambitious brokers reveals the dark side of economic success, which greed and the secrecy of a business partner you trust unconditionally can lead to.

li-7239875814874337280.title: Which five mistakes did the partners make in the folk tale The Turnip?
li-7239875814874337280.text: They did no planning, had uniform competences, named no coordinator, undervalued the smallest member (the mouse was called last) and never discussed scenarios. Regular partnership sessions are the place for such talks.

li-7239528074726301696.title: Why draw a portrait of the ideal partner before entering a partnership?
li-7239528074726301696.text: A portrait helps to assess your own abilities and needs soberly and to see what a partner could make up for. Partnerships usually grow out of friendship, family or work, and no more than 5% of businesspeople look for a partner deliberately.

li-7239194339808051201.title: Has there become too much AI in the information space?
li-7239194339808051201.text: While reading a text the author stumbled twice on the name AI-fred and remarks, jokingly, that there is now a great deal of AI in the information space.

li-7239155085744738304.title: Why plan scenarios if you cannot foresee everything?
li-7239155085744738304.text: "Unknown unknowns" cannot be foreseen, but there are "known unknowns", like toilet paper running out: they need no guessing, only an earlier agreement and a stock in reserve. This is how the author won over a sceptical partner.

li-7238900994430930946.title: Who in a partnership should make the decisions?
li-7238900994430930946.text: The one who will later have to fix the mistakes. This is the author's formula for the most emotional block of a partnership session: who decides, how, why that way and for how long.

li-7238793460680413184.title: Which five habits are sure to break a partnership apart?
li-7238793460680413184.text: Interrupting the partner, forgetting promises, taking company money without questions, taking time off without warning and sorting out disputes in front of the staff. The advice is given ironically, in reverse.

li-7237783863396073475.title: What does the illusion of self-organising partnerships hide?
li-7237783863396073475.text: Partners living in this illusion often fail to notice a conflict or a break-up coming. Hiding behind fears, intuition and an inner culture, they try to make the obvious invisible.

li-7237701473973768192.title: What does the film about Ray Kroc and McDonald's teach?
li-7237701473973768192.text: A biopic about Ray Kroc, who made McDonald's a globally recognised brand, teaches persistence and aggressive growth, and shows how important it is to find the right business partners.

li-7237360485291970560.title: Why is postponing a partnership session also a decision?
li-7237360485291970560.text: Underestimating inaction: "later" looks like a choice without consequences, yet it leads to a conversation under stress when conflict is already unavoidable. Better to hold the session with a specialist who is not emotionally involved.

li-7236985689165189123.title: What do concrete, measurable clauses of a partnership agreement look like?
li-7236985689165189123.text: Five sample clauses: hiring relatives above a $1,500 salary only with both partners’ consent, partner pay as the average of five matching résumés, 50 days of leave taken in turn, dividends after $1.5 million turnover, and a replacement for a departing partner.

li-7236614319973515265.title: How does a false dichotomy help dismiss an inconvenient argument?
li-7236614319973515265.text: It is the straw-man fallacy: the other side’s position is replaced by an extreme, absurd alternative while all other options are ignored. The author shows three forms in business dialogue: opposite swapped for contradiction, extreme conclusions and emotional manipulation.

li-7236251963280003072.title: Why is it better to agree with partners before a conflict?
li-7236251963280003072.text: Time spent protecting a business is unavoidable: on delicate talks before a conflict, or on courts and lawyers during one. An entrepreneur recalls partners spending a year and a half on 14 questions to write an “honour agreement” that later kept him in his own role.

li-7235179875030958082.title: What does the film about inventor Joy Mangano say about partnership?
li-7235179875030958082.text: A woman inventor built a successful business despite every difficulty. The film shows how motivation and perseverance overcome obstacles and makes plain how much negotiation skills and building partnerships matter.

li-7234815432396832769.title: Which three kinds of events should partners discuss in advance?
li-7234815432396832769.text: Per Noam Wasserman: the known, the known unknowns and the unknown unknowns. The first go into the agreement, the second get scenario planning, and the third need an independent outside party and shared principles and values.

li-7234454836992180225.title: What ritual helps partners stop talking shop outside work?
li-7234454836992180225.text: Spouses who co-own a business used a non-verbal sign: a vase in the hallway turned to the wall means no talk about work. A rival club’s flag in the office worked the same way for business partners, far better than the phrase “we need to talk”.

li-7234092552423907328.title: What is a conscious partnership?
li-7234092552423907328.text: A union in which each partner knows why a given rule exists and why they are in this partnership. The unconscious kind shows in phrases like “it just turned out that way” and charters downloaded from somewhere; conscious partners agree how to part in advance.

li-7233729235834568704.title: How do you get through to a partner who resists?
li-7233729235834568704.text: Sometimes a partner will not move and pushes back against every attempt to change things. The author holds that the power of intention and suitable approaches can at least get the partner to start listening.

li-7232643165848051712.title: What does the 2008 crisis film say about the right people at the right time?
li-7232643165848051712.text: A film based on real events: a few financial analysts foresaw the market crash and chose to profit from it. It shows how important it is to find the right people at the right time and see opportunity where others see only problems.

li-7232306365275246593.title: How can partners agree in advance on how they will clash?
li-7232306365275246593.text: The author offers a six-rule protocol for “we disagree, what do we do”: give arguments, do not interrupt, rely on facts rather than emotion, argue rested, probe the partner’s position, and decide nothing mid-dispute but return a day or two later.

li-7231923776114900992.title: What did partners settle when everyone and no one was in charge of finances?
li-7231923776114900992.text: A business run by three relatives and a close outsider appointed director had no shared strategy and erratic dividends. The session fixed a dividend policy, deadlines for strategy talks, shares, how partners present themselves and the decisions needing a “yes” from all four.

li-7231540894573723649.title: What do marriage contract and will statistics say about partnership agreements?
li-7231540894573723649.text: There are no figures on partnership agreements, so the author uses analogues: in the first half of 2024 marriages fell 15% while marriage contracts rose 33% (5.2% of marriages). Wills rose 16.2%: people write precise agreements down only when facing death.

li-7231204994367016960.title: Why does the author not share real cases and client references?
li-7231204994367016960.text: Work on partner relationships is covered by NDA, so real examples and references cannot be given. A public comment received after cases were worked through live with a group is all the more welcome.

li-7231189712781115392.title: Why do people refuse to take a helicopter view?
li-7231189712781115392.text: Once you learn what surrounds you, you can no longer ignore it, so many fear the height and the truth, like an ostrich burying its head in the sand. Hence flat-earthers using GPS and businessmen forming partnerships without a partnership agreement.

li-7230106441083219968.title: What does the film about Billy Beane say about building a team?
li-7230106441083219968.text: Baseball manager Billy Beane changes how he builds a team after meeting Yale graduate Peter Brand and his mathematical model. Together they lead the team to success and a so-called “eternal” record in the American league.

li-7229375062733164544.title: Should a conflict with a partner be settled by chat or in person?
li-7229375062733164544.text: The author gives an unconditional rule: in any conflict with a partner, do not chat, meet and talk. The rule comes without caveats or examples.

li-7229018233503203328.title: Why is it so hard for partners to start a talk about built-up discontent?
li-7229018233503203328.text: Such a talk may demand hard decisions, time and energy, and in the worst case a split. Delay is costly: clients and staff leave and the team suffers; the author proposes a partnership audit built on one-to-one interviews with each co-owner.

li-7228641983009837057.title: What insights did the author take from a partnership session outdoors?
li-7228641983009837057.text: A joking list of five “rules”, from never holding a session with naked people of different sexes to hoping all participants are alive, at least at the start. The joke plays on confusion with family constellations; the author closes by asking readers for tips.

li-7227554615666343937.title: What does the film about Howard Hughes say about business and partnership?
li-7227554615666343937.text: The biography of an aviator and entrepreneur who became a legend through his passion for innovation. The film shows how the pursuit of perfection and business can overcome any obstacle and touches deeply on business and personal partnerships.

li-7226829815142653952.title: How does the Thomas theorem explain rifts between partners?
li-7226829815142653952.text: If people define a situation as real, it is real in its consequences: one partner may read the other’s harmless act as a threat and start defending. Regular, structured dialogue, ideally a partnership session, keeps misunderstandings and discontent from piling up.

blog-sczenarnoe-planirovanie-v-partnersk.title: Why is scenario planning a safer bet than relying on luck?
blog-sczenarnoe-planirovanie-v-partnersk.text: Crediting others’ success to luck means giving up agency and any learning from mistakes. A scenario played out in advance removes negotiation in a crisis: Chicago imposed quarantine earlier while New York missed its moment. Luck wins once; a system wins repeatedly.

li-7226482530474987520.title: What happened to an investor who had no written agreement?
li-7226482530474987520.text: When the product made millions, the specialist partner decided he could have managed without the investor and proposed simply returning the money. Alignment and an agreement must come while you are still of value to the partner: expertise, money, connections or sales.

li-7226112349051490305.title: What is your favorite way to recover quickly?
li-7226112349051490305.text: A short question to readers: everyone has their own way of recovering quickly, and the author asks for their favorite.

li-7225071572846317571.title: Can the break-up of a partnership benefit a whole industry?
li-7225071572846317571.text: The brothers Adi and Rudi began as partners, but accumulated disagreements split them, and each founded a major sports brand: Adidas and Puma. The film shows how clashing ambitions and competition can drive an entire industry forward.

li-7224670664304046080.title: What does “I am responsible for logistics” actually mean?
li-7224670664304046080.text: On its own the phrase means nothing: it sounds clear, so the listener agrees and moves on. A written partnership agreement guards against such vague statements, because partners writing it down avoid empty phrases themselves.

li-7223950908680769537.title: What did the author cover at the workshop for the business community The Club?
li-7223950908680769537.text: A workshop on business partnership that the author gave by invitation to the members of the business community The Club.

li-7223945878430969857.title: How do you resolve a conflict with the FAVER technique from Stanford?
li-7223945878430969857.text: Five first-person steps: name your emotions, ask yourself “what” triggered them, assume the other person means no harm, discuss the facts with I-statements, and part without hostility. The technique is taught at Stanford Medical School.

li-7223593998316105728.title: How different can partners be and still work together?
li-7223593998316105728.text: Very different: partners can differ significantly from each other, the main thing is that they “look in the same direction”.

li-7222496232659681282.title: Can an agreement on a napkin last to the end of a partnership?
li-7222496232659681282.text: It can, if real actions reinforce it again and again: in the film “Gold”, agreements made on a napkin were fulfilled to the end. The real-life plot rests on unconditional belief in the business, dedication and trust between the partners.

li-7221771580995956737.title: Which two scenarios should partners be ready for in advance?
li-7221771580995956737.text: Failure and “carnival”, meaning runaway success. For failure, agree in advance in what proportion partners add money and at what indicators to close the project; for success, how each partner can be sure he will not be squeezed out.

li-7221409115456077829.title: How can a top manager prepare to ask for a stake in the business?
