li-7221409115456077829.text: Sooner or later a top manager has to ask for a stake in the business he runs, and an outside view helps. The author prepares the negotiation strategy for such talks and has put together a guide for preparing on your own.

li-7221045929133416449.title: How do you recover after an extremely demanding working week?
li-7221045929133416449.text: A short personal note: water at +2 °C as an extreme recovery after an extreme working week.

li-7219606014038261761.title: Why does a partnership rarely turn out the way it was imagined?
li-7219606014038261761.text: Every partnership starts as a mental image, and that image is only preliminary: once partners move to implementation, things often do not go as imagined. How to make the partnership bear fruit is covered at the linked page.

li-7219234835603591168.title: When should you take someone on as a partner, and when is it better not to?
li-7219234835603591168.text: If a partnership can be avoided, it should be: first hire the person, get consulting from them, ask them to mentor you, find someone else with the same resources, or rethink your model. If none of that works, a partnership taken on consciously will be stronger.

li-7218887639846780929.title: Is an agreement on a napkin enough to consider the matter settled?
li-7218887639846780929.text: No: three co-owners believed they had agreed, but their points, “the majority decides”, “until things are normal” and “no nonsense”, left open who counts as the majority of three and normal for whom. At the partnership session everything was spelled out.

blog-ot-idei-k-ustojchivomu-partnerstvu.title: Why are friendship, enthusiasm and trust not enough for a lasting partnership?
blog-ot-idei-k-ustojchivomu-partnerstvu.text: The image of the partnership a person brings into the group differs from reality, and that tension has to be resolved through negotiation and detailed agreements in the form of a partnership agreement. Groups without them survive more by luck than by skill.

li-7218520749421056000.title: Why does friendship between founders not prevent conflict over roles and money?
li-7218520749421056000.text: Wozniak and Jobs, the co-founders of Apple, could not discuss roles and compensation, and these issues stayed unresolved throughout their work together. Wasserman, in “The Founder’s Dilemmas”, notes that when co-founders avoid pressing topics, internal tension builds up.

li-7217443189958275072.title: Which uncomfortable questions should you ask partners before you start?
li-7217443189958275072.text: The ones our culture avoids so as not to “scare off” the venture: how often one can take a vacation, whose departure would end the business, what happens to the knowledge base on parting. Without them, agreements stay flat, like a stage character without a thousand questions.

li-7217074780624060417.title: Why do an ex-corporate executive and a founder read events differently?
li-7217074780624060417.text: Each has a different idea of what is appropriate and a different way of approaching tasks, so partners perceive events differently, weigh them differently and assess them differently. This breeds disagreement; the author covers the roots of the problem at the link.

li-7216712471594582016.title: What should a partner be like, according to Arkady Moreynis?
li-7216712471594582016.text: Disagree on about half of the issues at the start, share the same level of ambition and learn at the same pace. The author retells this list, notes that it is incomplete, and invites readers to add to it.

blog-raznoglasiya-s-partnyorom-sinhroniz.title: How can partners synchronise their pictures of the world when these diverge?
blog-raznoglasiya-s-partnyorom-sinhroniz.text: The divergence itself is not the problem: the problem is maladaptation, when the gap between reality and private notions of it grows too large. A partnership session with a facilitator synchronises the partners, and its result is a partnership agreement.

li-7216075246771007488.title: Who does a professional work with?
li-7216075246771007488.text: With professionals: the author holds that being a professional means working with professionals, and names a specific agency as one of them.

li-7215988450896838659.title: What should partners do if one of them drops out after a personal tragedy?
li-7215988450896838659.text: Agree on a scenario in advance. Partners come up with different solutions: a psychologist paid by the company, a long leave with agreements preserved, a mandatory month away from the business, or an open discussion of adequacy and satisfaction with the work.

li-7214529287087939586.title: What if one partner carries the suitcase and the money is split evenly?
li-7214529287087939586.text: In a joke about two friends splitting money fifty-fifty, the one who carries the suitcase eventually falls into depression: the effort is unequal, the share is equal. The author advises defining and fixing each side’s position in the partnership.

li-7214171988993454081.title: Why is admitting what you do not know the first step to professionalism?
li-7214171988993454081.text: A fixed mindset creates an urgency to prove yourself over and over and blocks development. As Carol Dweck cites it, NASA rejects candidates with spotless records and prefers those who failed significantly and recovered.

li-7213797637811015680.title: Why is formalising partnership agreements linked to stress?
li-7213797637811015680.text: People are often significant irritants to each other, so the importance of formalised partnership agreements for co-owners is hard to overestimate. The body’s response algorithm to irritants is covered in the linked article.

blog-kortizol-i-partnerstvo.title: Why does the lack of an agreement keep co-owners in constant anxiety?
blog-kortizol-i-partnerstvo.text: One person is a super-stimulus to another: the reticular formation wakes the body in hundredths of a second and cortisol readies it to fight or flee. Without formalised agreements a partner remains a source of threat, and the response stays on for years.

li-7211642709218893827.title: Whom to pick as a partner: a solid average performer or a flamboyant founder?
li-7211642709218893827.text: Candidate A is successful but has neither extraordinary achievements nor significant failures; candidate B has two bankruptcies, three successful ventures, connections and status. B looks better at first glance, but the author says choosing him is most likely a mistake.

blog-upravlenie-razocharovaniem-v-partne.title: How can partners manage disappointment in a business partnership?
blog-upravlenie-razocharovaniem-v-partne.text: Disappointment is expectation minus reality, so the closer expectations are to reality, the weaker it is. The main tool is systematic communication: partners immersing each other in the context, so that disappointment does not grow into resentment, anger and a broken bond.

blog-razlichiya-czelej-v-partnerstve.title: What are the five different kinds of goals partners can share?
blog-razlichiya-czelej-v-partnerstve.text: Similar, identical, common, joint and unified goals are not synonyms: they run from a close vision of the result to a full merging of effort. Partners find out which kind they really have most easily in regular partnership sessions; the author illustrates it with buying cars.

blog-partner-a-ili-partner-v.title: Why is a flamboyant entrepreneur a risky choice of partner?
blog-partner-a-ili-partner-v.text: We tend to credit more potential to someone who talks a lot, sounds confident and is always busy, and we miss the huge swings of his career. A solid, crisis-free middle performer is the safer bet, and a partner profile drawn up before joining helps to judge the fit.

blog-konczy-v-vodu-ili-izmenenie-partner.title: What happens to a business if one of the partners suddenly dies?
blog-konczy-v-vodu-ili-izmenenie-partner.text: Without a partnership agreement the remaining co-owners cannot prove what was settled: after the director died, over half of receivables and payables were in cash, and the documents and money access were with him. Write down scenarios for the "unforeseen" in advance.

li-7209485166027694083.title: Are joint, common and unified goals really the same thing?
li-7209485166027694083.text: No: similar goals share a direction, common goals matter to everyone, joint goals are reached by combined effort, and unified goals merge interests into one. The author shows each type with a car-buying example; regular partnership sessions help tell them apart.

li-7208726970065428481.title: Can partners prepare in advance for the sudden death of a co-owner?
li-7208726970065428481.text: Yes: scenarios for "unforeseen" events should be discussed and put on paper, with an independent expert if experience is lacking. In the case described, four co-owners without an agreement had no proof of settlements, and the company's life changed in a single day.

li-7207639488162938880.title: How can partners reduce the potential for disappointment?
li-7207639488162938880.text: By systematically bringing each other into the context: the closer expectations are to reality, the less disappointment. Each partner owns what they control and brings the rest to joint discussion, so the disappointment is aimed at the situation, not at a partner.

li-7207300810928533505.title: How does disappointment build up in a partnership?
li-7207300810928533505.text: A partner hides the real state of affairs to spare the other, creates an illusion of control, or promises more than they can deliver. Meeting reality brings shock and undermines trust, even when it all began with good intentions.

li-7207022073343311872.title: What does Churchill's 1940 speech teach about managing expectations?
li-7207022073343311872.text: The speech about "blood, toil, tears and sweat" set expectations without illusions: any outcome better than promised is a victory, and a worse turn is understandable and foreseeable. The author contrasts it with today's politicians, who inflate expectations.

li-7206932948007153664.title: Which business situations inevitably disappoint partners?
li-7206932948007153664.text: Limited resources, client demands and the market create situations beyond partners' control: no funds for one partner's project, no full dividends, changed roles, cut funding for a business line. Partners need to be able to identify and soften this disappointment.

li-7206594349315371008.title: What is the formula for disappointment?
li-7206594349315371008.text: Disappointment arises where there is expectation and anticipation of victory, but poor awareness of the actual situation and no ability to control it.

li-7206581156241121280.title: What is disappointment made of?
li-7206581156241121280.text: Disappointment is the negative result of the operation "expectation minus reality". Psychology, sociology, management and partnership theory all study expectations, but life inevitably confronts them with reality, and unmet expectations lead to disappointment.

li-7206242726516862978.title: How can disappointment be described mathematically?
li-7206242726516862978.text: Disappointment is the negative result of a subtraction: expectation minus reality. To manage it, one has to understand how it arises.

li-7205919078715166720.title: Why is disappointment dangerous for a business partnership?
li-7205919078715166720.text: Disappointment breeds resentment, anger or despair and sets off the "Four Horsemen" that destroy relationships: contempt, criticism, stonewalling and threats. Partners therefore need to know its causes and manage it, not only expectations.

blog-doverie-fundament-ekonomicheskogo-u.title: How much does trust determine economic success?
blog-doverie-fundament-ekonomicheskogo-u.text: In Yann Algan's research, about 45% of the variation in per-capita income is explained by the effect of trust. Trust in business rests on contracts, and for co-owners on a partnership agreement worked out in a partnership session.

li-7203555224341352448.title: Can the effect of trust on national wealth be measured?
li-7203555224341352448.text: Yes: using General Social Survey data, Yann Algan estimated that trust explains about 45% of the variation in per-capita income. For co-owners, trust rests on a partnership agreement discussed against an exhaustive list of issues.
